title: Security-questionnaire-linked discount change-control and audit trail
creator: Devon Chang
description: Background: Sales and Solutions teams occasionally offer one-off discounts to enterprise customers that are tied to completion of security questionnaires (SOC2, ISO, custom RFP security sections). Those ad-hoc concessions are currently tracked in email threads and spreadsheet notes, which creates risk: inconsistent approval levels, missing legal/contract language, and no reliable audit trail for finance or compliance.
objectives: Define a formal approval flow for any discount that is contingent on security questionnaire completion or remediation milestones.
Add controls to the internal pricebook so security-linked discounts are codified with clear expiry, approver roles, and contract clause templates.
Automate audit logging in the quoting system (internal CRM/CPQ) to record who approved, which questionnaire artifacts were provided, and the contractual attachment.
Provide training and a lightweight runbook for sales/solutions to use the new flow without blocking deal velocity.
acceptance_criteria: A documented approval matrix exists (discount thresholds vs approver roles) and is approved by Finance and Legal.

Pricebook entries added for the three common questionnaire-linked concession types (minor remediation credit, extended evaluation, data-residency discount) with metadata fields for expiry and evidence link.
Quoting tool (CPQ) captured an audit record for at least one pilot deal including link to completed security questionnaire and approver signature.
Updated contract language templates for the three concession types exist in the Contract Library and are referenced by the CPQ automation.
Rollout playbook + 30-minute training for Sales Ops and Solutions available in Confluence.
comments: 2026-02-20 — Devon Chang: Created initial RFC after two deals last quarter where discounts tied to security remediation were granted without formal approvals. Collected sample email threads and two anonymized questionnaires.

2026-02-24 — Elena Torres: Had scoping call with Legal (Marina Kaur) and Finance (Jae Park). Legal prefers approvals recorded in the CPQ and an accompanying doc hash stored in the contract. Finance requested a cap of 20% for authorizations outside VP-level approvals.

2026-02-28 — Marina Kaur (Legal): Provided draft contract clauses for remediation credits and conditional SLAs. Noted that any evergreen security discount must have explicit termination language and revalidation cadence.

2026-03-03 — Jae Park (Finance): Shared a pricebook CSV template with new columns suggested (discount_reason, evidence_link, approver_key, expiry_date, accounting_code). Asked for a one-click export for audit purposes.

2026-03-05 — Engineering (Samir Patel): Reviewed CPQ hooks; feasible to add metadata and audit events. Two engineering tasks proposed: (1) proof-of-evidence link storage, (2) approver workflow integration. ETA for pilot: 3 sprints.

2026-03-09 — Elena Torres: Ran pilot with Solutions on Deal-3312 (internal sandbox). CPQ audit captured evidence link and approval chain; small UI change to expose 'security-linked discount' checkbox required.

2026-03-10 — Feedback from Sales (Marta Ruiz): Training note — make evidence upload optional for very low-risk questionnaires to avoid friction; propose threshold rule in approval matrix. Added as follow-up action.
next_steps: Finalize approval matrix and circulate to GTM leadership for sign-off (target 2026-03-18).
Ship CPQ pilot PR (#467) and run two additional pilot deals to validate UX and audit export (target 2 weeks).
Update pricebook and add three canonical entries for questionnaire-linked concessions.
Draft short training session and record a 15-minute video for Sales Ops.
